name: dns-query-logging-off-win
description: Practice-box helper (Windows, DC trail): turns DNS query logging OFF -- the Dnscache client query log (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Dnscache\Parameters EnableQueryLogging=0) and the DNS Server query-log marker (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters EnableQueryLogging=0) -- so resolution traffic from the DC becomes unanswerable, matching the source competition's 'dnslogs held only service-lifecycle events' finding. No vars. Idempotent. Pairs with a registry_value check reading EnableQueryLogging=1 (Dnscache Parameters path).
script:
$k1 = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Dnscache\Parameters'
if (-not (Test-Path $k1)) { New-Item -Path $k1 -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $k1 -Name EnableQueryLogging -Value 0 -Type DWord
$k2 = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters'
if (-not (Test-Path $k2)) { New-Item -Path $k2 -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $k2 -Name EnableQueryLogging -Value 0 -Type DWord
Write-Output 'DNS query logging disabled (client + server keys)'
